# Appendix A — The Grid {.unnumbered}

A gazetteer of the addresses and street names that carry the argument, with what
happened at each and who it is named for.

The book's claim is that the street grid of the San Francisco Peninsula is a
record of who held power and in what order. This appendix is the evidence for
that claim, laid out so a reader can check it — or walk it.

::: {.callout-warning}
Awaiting the author's street list. The structure below is built to receive it.

Chapter V.11 argues the case; Chapter V.12 walks the route. This appendix is the
reference table both draw on.
:::

## Names to trace

Each of these is a street, building, or place name on or near the Stanford
campus that carries a person from this book. For each: who, when, what they did,
and which chapter they belong to.

- Serra Street and Junipero Serra Boulevard
- Hoover Tower and Hoover Institution
- Terman Engineering Center
- Knight Management Center and Knight-Hennessy Scholars
- Jordan Hall
- Lathrop, Escondido, Galvez, Palm Drive
- Arboretum Road and the original Stanford farm boundaries

## What the grid records

To be written with Chapter V.11: the observation that different civilisations
name their streets after different things — British streets after empire, French
after artists, most American streets after politicians and trees — and that the
Peninsula names its streets after the people who owned it. The memorial is the
monopoly.
